baseline.function: Allow one simulation round to pass at the current position.
Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
Place owned units on the ground.
Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
baseline.args: name, function, conditions, inputs, costs, effects

baseline.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
Give a name of up to 60 characters to this place (empty subject) or to a visible object or nearby item; naming the same subject again replaces your name for it.
Leave a mark or inscription of up to 120 characters on the ground here (empty subject) or on an object or item within reach.
Say up to 240 characters aloud; everyone living within 5 units hears it, seen or not.
Invite listeners to meet at a place and a later round within 200 rounds, with an optional note of up to 120 characters.
baseline.args: x: number, y: number, round: integer>=1, text

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progr
Prepare whole units of your own food without heat, water or tools: each paid round checks one held unit by eye, brushes it by hand and moves it into your prepared lot; inspect food
Lay one carried loose unit on clear ground within reach at a chosen point and angle, as a ground item anyone can pick up; inspect the unit and site first.

execution.progress: Three paid one-round stages; job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stages after revalidation; completion, failure, cancelling and death settle once. Growth runs only in ordinary simulation.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
details.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Paid one-unit rounds; job, input, unit outcomes and lot persist across pauses; resuming pays only the remaining units after revalidation; completion, an unsuitable unit, cancelling and death settle once. No unattended progress.

details.costs: Study: 2 rounds. Prepare: inputStackId is the exact item id of your own edible food stack, quantity the whole units to prepare (at most its whole units); one round and 0.5 energy per unit, so 7 units take 7 rounds and 3.5 energy. Every round is checked before any charge; prepare resumes your paused work (inputStackId and quantity may be omitted). Inspect (inputStackId of your own food) and inspect-progress (your latest preparation): one round, 0.2 energy, no food used. Cancel: one round, no energy. No vessel, water, fuel, tool or ground surface is used or given. Eating and giving use eat and give at their own costs.
details.effects: Each paid round separates one whole unit from the input, checks it by eye and brushes it by hand, held, never set on the ground. A usable unit joins one owned lot of the same food with unchanged quantity, origin, age, decay, nutrition and toxicity, recorded as raw, unheated, dry-brushed, safety unknown. Loose soil on food is not represented, so no debris is measured or removed and no cleanliness is claimed. A spoiled unit is reported unsuitable, stays unprepared and ends the work. Nothing is cooked, peeled, washed, made safe or kept fresher; food keeps ageing, and the planting trial treats prepared units as processed. The lot holds only completed units. Inspections record visible condition, treatment and your own eating record (not a safety test) as an unverified personal record. An unworked round, too little energy, or an input no longer yours with a whole unit pauses without charge. Cancel or death ends the work; completed units stay. No refund or reward; nobody is fed.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Thermal food preparation
value.function: Assess whether your own food could be heat-treated: one paid look records its visible condition and treatment and which supplied or reachable prerequisites (heat source, support, tool, vessel, water, evidence) are present, unverified or missing. Heating is unavailable in this world version and is refused at no cost.
value.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Assess: inputStackId is the exact item id of your own unreserved food, quantity the amount considered (0.1 steps; default all of it); one round and 0.2 energy. No food, fuel, tool, vessel or water is used, moved or reserved. Optional sourceId, apparatusIds (up to 4 exact ids of your items, ground items or objects within reach) and evidenceKey (an exact key of your own records) are only checked. Heat: refused before any cost. A wrong id, non-food, too large a quantity or energy below 0.2 fails at no cost.
value.effects: Assess writes an unverified personal record and an event: the food quantity, origin, age, decay, visible condition and treatment records; your own eating record of that food (not a test of this stack); for each supplied id whether it is absent or present (a source with or without represented heat, otherwise role unverified); any object within reach with available heat; water in your cell; whether the evidence key exists; and the missing prerequisites. It never labels food cooked, edible or safe: safety stays unknown, and heat would not prove edibility or remove hazards. It does not show that no heat source exists elsewhere. Nothing changes except your energy and records. No reward.

execution.progress: One atomic paid assessment round; only the personal record persists. Heating never starts, so there is no work to pause, resume or cancel.

retrieval.access: Search/index only; omission is not absence. Use exact ids and zero-based offset/part for full records. No physical observation, state change or reward is performed.
